outputDir.why: THE ACT BINDING, and the one fact that says WHICH act this per-GAME document governs. The consumer reads one input file and writes zone_bg.bin / bg_tiles.bin / bg_anim.emp / bg_anim_banks.bin into ONE hardcoded directory, so the document describes exactly the act whose generated data lives there — not every act in the project. Nothing inside the document names an act; this literal is the whole of the binding, which is why it is vendored here rather than inferred. Aurora matches it against project.json's per-act `stripPath` (the same project-root-relative directory) and treats a project whose acts point elsewhere as having NO overridden act — the safe direction, since the document then governs nothing Aurora is showing. SEAM, reported to aeon: the pairing is a coincidence of two hardcodes, one per repo. Closing it means aeon deriving OUT_DIR from project.json (or naming the act in the document) rather than both sides spelling the same path.
authorities: aeon tools/inject_editor_bg.py — `OUT_DIR = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..', 'games', 'sonic4', 'data', 'generated', 'ojz', 'act1')`, and every write in `main()` is `os.path.join(OUT_DIR, ...)`: zone_bg.bin, bg_tiles.bin, bg_anim.emp, bg_anim_banks.bin, ojz_palette.bin

aeon tools/regenerate-level.sh — `if [[ -f games/sonic4/data/editor_bg_override.json ]]; then python3 "${TOOLS}/inject_editor_bg.py"; fi`, run with the repo root as cwd, which is what makes OUT_DIR project-root-relative
outputDir.note: DRIFT DISCLOSED, NOT RE-VENDORED (aurora, 2026-09-03, reading aeon 3a4712faa920100653669c1ec3fc26c2da71ef68). `OUT_DIR` and the input path are no longer hardcoded literals: aeon's `BgActNames.out_dir()` derives games/sonic4/data/generated/<zone_id>/<act_id> and `BgActNames.override_path()` derives the input file, both from project.json's zone/act INDICES (defaults zone 0 / act 0). BOTH LITERALS BELOW STILL HOLD FOR THE DEFAULT ACT — `LEGACY_OVERRIDE_ACT = ('ojz', 'act1')` keeps that one act on the un-suffixed editor_bg_override.json, and its out_dir is exactly this string — so nothing in this codec is wrong today. What changed is the KIND of fact: the pairing is no longer two hardcodes but one hardcode against one derivation, and a project whose first act is not ojz/act1 would break the match. Re-vendoring that half is its own parcel; it is recorded here rather than silently corrected because a stale citation is worse than a stale value.

BGANIM_MAX_BANDS.why: The band ceiling. NOT pinned from prose: read out of all THREE deliberate authorities, which agree at 4. Raising it is a three-file engine change and never a writer decision.
authorities: aeon engine/system/constants.emp:212 — `pub const BGANIM_MAX_BANDS = 4`; sizes engine/ram.emp:526 `BgAnim_LastStep: [u16; BGANIM_MAX_BANDS]`

aeon engine/level/bg_anim.emp — `const BGANIM_MAX_BANDS = 4`, a DELIBERATE module-local mirror (the file is lowered standalone by bg_anim_port against an empty symbol table, so it may not import engine.constants); bounds the DEBUG-only runtime assert
aeon tools/inject_editor_bg.py — `BGANIM_MAX_BANDS = 4`, the emitter cap and the RELEASE defense (`assert len(anims) <= BGANIM_MAX_BANDS`)
BGANIM_MAX_BANDS.aeonGate: aeon tools/test_bg_emit.py::TestBgAnimBandCeiling::test_all_three_authorities_agree — reads all three and fails on disagreement

BGANIM_PHASE_BANKS.why: `phases` carries EXACTLY this many banks — not at most, not at least. Pre-shifted art 1px apart; the fine phase is `step & 7`.
authorities: aeon engine/level/bg_anim.emp — `const BGANIM_BANKS = 8` and `banks: [*u8; BGANIM_BANKS]` in `struct bganim_band`

aeon tools/inject_editor_bg.py — `assert len(b['bank_offsets']) == 8, 'bganim_band.banks is [*u8; 8]: each band needs exactly 8 phases'`, and `bank_offsets` is built `for ph in range(len(a['phases']))`, so 8 phases in is the only input that satisfies it

BG_TILE_CAPACITY.why: `len(tiles) <= BG_TILE_CAPACITY`. The nominal 512 is wrong — the sprite table ($B800) and HScroll table ($BC00) sit in the top of the $8000-$BFFF region.
authorities: aeon tools/vram_map.py:26 — `BG_TILE_CAPACITY = 448`, GENERATED from games/sonic4/vram.toml (the one authority; the four-copies-of-448 incident is why inject_editor_bg.py imports it rather than restating it)
aeon tools/inject_editor_bg.py — `assert len(tiles) <= BG_TILE_CAPACITY`

BG_TILE_BASE_SLOT.why: Not enforced by this codec — recorded because it is what makes the PREFIX identity an identity: a band's DMA destination is BG_TILE_BASE_VRAM + slot_base*32 with BG_TILE_BASE_VRAM = $8000, and 1024 * 32 = $8000 IS the tile blob's own base. So slot 0 is literally tiles[0]; bands DMA OVER the static blob's leading slots, never beside them.
authorities: aeon tools/vram_map.py:25 — `BG_TILE_BASE_SLOT = 1024`
aeon tools/inject_editor_bg.py — `BG_TILE_BASE_VRAM = 0x8000`; `vram_dest = BG_TILE_BASE_VRAM + b['slot_base'] * 32`; and the layout rebase `(idx + BG_TILE_BASE_SLOT) & 0x7FF`

TILE_BYTES.why: One 8x8 4bpp tile. `col_bytes = rows * TILE_BYTES` is the quantity required to be a power of two.
authorities: aeon tools/inject_editor_bg.py — `col_bytes = rows * 32`
aeon engine/level/bg_anim.emp — `const TILE_BYTES_SHIFT = 5  // log2(32 bytes per 8x8 tile)`

TILE_PIXELS.why: Each tile in `tiles` and in every `phases` bank is a flat array of exactly this many pixel values, row-major 8x8.
authorities: aeon tools/inject_editor_bg.py — the pack loop `for row in range(8): for col in range(4)` indexes `t[row*8 + col*2]` and `t[row*8 + col*2 + 1]`, whose highest index is 63

TILE_PIXEL_MAX.why: 4bpp. The consumer MASKS rather than rejects (`hi = t[...] & 0xF`), so a 16 bakes silently as a 0 — which is why the writer refuses out-of-range instead of relying on the mask.
authorities: aeon tools/inject_editor_bg.py — `hi = t[row*8 + col*2] & 0xF`
empyrean docs/AURORA_EFFECTS_SCHEMA.md §5 — writer-normative: `each tile = cols*rows tiles, each tile = 64 pixel values 0..15`

TILE_WIDTH_PX.why: `pattern_px` must equal `cols * TILE_WIDTH_PX` — the pattern's width in pixels, from which the consumer derives `step_mask = pattern_px - 1`.
authorities: aeon tools/inject_editor_bg.py — `assert pattern_px == cols * 8, 'pattern width must equal cols*8'`

BG_LAYOUT_WORDS.why: 64x64 nametable words, the post-pad length the consumer asserts.
authorities: aeon tools/inject_editor_bg.py — `assert len(layout) == 4096, 'layout must be 64x32 or 64x64 words'`; `COLS, ROWS = 64, 64`

BG_LAYOUT_WORDS_LEGACY.why: 64x32. The consumer ZERO-PADS it to 4096 rather than refusing, so a legacy file is legal input. This codec accepts it and does NOT rewrite it: silently re-lengthening someone's layout is an unrequested edit, and the pad is the consumer's business.
authorities: aeon tools/inject_editor_bg.py — `if len(layout) == 2048: layout = layout + [0]*2048  # legacy 32-row layout: pad to 64 rows`

LAYOUT_WORD_MAX.why: Each layout entry is packed big-endian unsigned 16-bit; anything outside 0..65535 raises inside the consumer rather than baking.
authorities: aeon tools/inject_editor_bg.py — `struct.pack_into('>H', nt, (col * ROWS + row) * 2, word)`

LAYOUT_TILE_INDEX_MASK.why: The low bits of a layout word hold the BLOB-LOCAL tile index; every bit above them is the Genesis nametable's own attribute field (priority / palette line / flips), which the consumer PRESERVES verbatim. A writer that renumbers `tiles` must therefore rewrite `word & LAYOUT_TILE_INDEX_MASK` and leave `word & ~LAYOUT_TILE_INDEX_MASK` alone. THE ESCAPE MATTERS AS MUCH AS THE MASK: the consumer rebases only `if word != 0`, so a layout word of EXACTLY zero is passed through unrebased and renders VRAM tile 0 (blank) — it does NOT mean tiles[0]. A renumbering that turns a nonzero word into zero, or a zero word into nonzero, silently changes what that cell renders while every other assert in the consumer still passes.
authorities: aeon tools/inject_editor_bg.py — the nametable loop: `if word != 0: idx = word & 0x7FF; word = (word & ~0x7FF) | ((idx + BG_TILE_BASE_SLOT) & 0x7FF)`

drivers.$comment: aeon tools/inject_editor_bg.py — `DRIVERS = {'camera_x': 0, 'camera_y': 1, 'timer': 2}`, mirrored by engine/level/bg_anim.emp's `driver` field doc (0 = Camera_X, 1 = Camera_Y, 2 = Logic_Tick low word). A driver names the SCALAR SOURCE only and NEVER an axis: `camera_y` does NOT mean vertical motion, and it is the name that reads like a vertical instruction and is not one. Which way a band moves is the `axis` key (default "horizontal"), added 2026-09-02 at aeon 3a4712faa920100653669c1ec3fc26c2da71ef68; before that every band moved horizontally, and this comment said so — the sentence is retired, not softened.

topLevelKeys.$comment: Declaration order IS the canonical write order (aeon EFFECTS_CONSUMER_CONTRACT.md §1.1 table order). `ownership` is Aurora's, per the 2026-08-22 sole-writer ruling (aurora docs/reviews/2026-08-22-bg-override-ownership-ruling.md §5; empyrean AURORA_EFFECTS_SCHEMA.md §5.2).

layout.cite: inject_editor_bg.py — `layout, tiles = data['layout'], data['tiles']`, then the row-major -> column-major transpose

tiles.cite: inject_editor_bg.py — `data['tiles']`, capacity-asserted and packed into bg_tiles.bin

anims.cite: inject_editor_bg.py — `anims = data.get('anims')`; absent or falsy -> the disabled stub (band_count = 0)
anims.emptyIsUnauthored: aeon tools/test_bg_emit.py::TestBgAnimBandCoherence::test_live_override_file_is_coherent_if_it_has_bands asserts `assertNotIn('anims', live)` when there are no bands, with the reason 'an empty `anims` key is neither absent nor authored'. That binds the WRITER: Aurora never emits an empty array. It does NOT bind the reader — inject_editor_bg.py bakes such a document as the disabled stub without complaint, so refusing to open it would make Aurora unable to load a file its own consumer accepts. The reader therefore DROPS the key and reports it in notices; the refusal lives on the write path, which is the boundary that can enforce it. The single exception is an empty `anims` beside a legacy `anim`: the consumer's fallback is keyed on `anims is None`, so an empty array suppresses it and the band is silently dropped — there the emptiness is load-bearing and normalizing would be a guess, so the reader refuses.

anim.cite: inject_editor_bg.py — `if anims is None and data.get('anim'): anims = [data['anim']]`
anim.writerRule: aeon EFFECTS_CONSUMER_CONTRACT.md §1.1: 'LEGACY single-band form … Writers must not emit it (read-side compatibility only)'. This codec therefore UPGRADES it on read (anim -> anims[0]) and refuses to serialize a document still carrying it — the only behaviour that neither emits the legacy key nor destroys the band it holds.

palette.notValidatedHere: Aurora does not own this key, so it does not judge it. Refusing a file over a key whose constraint belongs to someone else (and which the drift rule lets them change) would block an author from opening a file its owner considers fine.

bandKeys.$comment: Each element of `anims`. aeon EFFECTS_CONSUMER_CONTRACT.md §1.2; declaration order is that table's order and is the canonical write order for a band.

cols.cite: inject_editor_bg.py — `cols, rows = a['cols'], a['rows']`; on a HORIZONTAL band `cols` is `_AXIS_PERIOD_TILES` and `pattern_px == cols*8`, while on a VERTICAL band `cols` is `_AXIS_UNIT_TILES` and `band_axis_geometry` asserts `(1 << unit_shift) == cols*32`

rows.cite: inject_editor_bg.py — `cols, rows = a['cols'], a['rows']`; on a HORIZONTAL band `rows` is `_AXIS_UNIT_TILES` and `band_axis_geometry` asserts `(1 << unit_shift) == rows*32`, while on a VERTICAL band `rows` is `_AXIS_PERIOD_TILES` and `pattern_px == rows*8`

axis.cite: inject_editor_bg.py — `axis = a.get('axis', 'horizontal')` in `band_axis_geometry`, refused by name against `BAND_AXES = ('horizontal', 'vertical')`; `unitKey`/`periodKey` are its `_AXIS_UNIT_TILES` / `_AXIS_PERIOD_TILES` tables verbatim
axis.why: Which way the band's pattern TRANSLATES. NOT the same thing as `driver`, which names the SCALAR the step is read from and never an axis. The engine is axis-agnostic and always was — `col_shift` is log2 of the rotation UNIT in bytes and `step_mask` is the period in px minus 1 — so the vertical arm reuses the same whole-unit DMA rotate with no engine byte changed. Direction is fixed and is NOT a key: an increasing driver scrolls a horizontal band LEFT and a vertical band UP.

pattern_px.cite: inject_editor_bg.py — `assert pattern_px == period_px` where `band_axis_geometry` returns `period_tiles * 8`: cols*8 on a horizontal band, rows*8 on a vertical one

driver.cite: inject_editor_bg.py — `DRIVERS[a.get('driver', 'camera_x')]`; an unlisted name is a KeyError at bake

slot_base.cite: inject_editor_bg.py — `slot_base = a.get('slot_base', slot_cursor)`; `assert slot_base == slot_cursor, 'bands must pack contiguously from slot 0'`

phases.cite: inject_editor_bg.py — `for bank in a['phases']: assert len(bank) == n`, and validate_band_coherence's `phases[0] == tiles[base:base+n]`

invariants.rotationUnitPowerOfTwo: The band's ROTATION UNIT in bytes must be a power of two — rows * TILE_BYTES on a horizontal band, cols * TILE_BYTES on a vertical one (aeon `band_axis_geometry`: `unit_bytes = a[_AXIS_UNIT_TILES[axis]] * 32`, `unit_shift = unit_bytes.bit_length() - 1`, `assert (1 << unit_shift) == unit_bytes`). The rule keeps its SHAPE across the axes — the runtime rotates a whole unit by SHIFTING — and changes only which band key it is spelled on. Was `columnBytesPowerOfTwo`, which stated the horizontal reading as if it were the only one.
invariants.patternPeriod: pattern_px == the period ALONG THE AXIS: cols * TILE_WIDTH_PX on a horizontal band, rows * TILE_WIDTH_PX on a vertical one (aeon `band_axis_geometry` returns `period_tiles * 8`; `main()` asserts `pattern_px == period_px`). Was `patternWidth`, which is the horizontal name for it.
invariants.contiguousPacking: bands pack contiguously from slot 0 in list order; slot_base, when present, must equal the running cursor
invariants.insideTheBlob: slot_base + cols*rows <= len(tiles) for every band
invariants.prefixIdentity: phases[0] == tiles[slot_base : slot_base + cols*rows] — the band's rest state IS the static tiles it covers. This is the invariant that makes anims/tiles/layout ONE unit rather than three separable keys: a violation bakes CLEANLY and ships silently corrupt art, and every other assert in the consumer still passes (aeon docs/BUGS.md TOOL-01; tools/bg_override_io.py's docstring; aeon tools/test_bg_emit.py::TestBgAnimBandCoherence).
invariants.capacity: len(tiles) <= BG_TILE_CAPACITY. Animated slots are a PREFIX of tiles, NOT an addition — they cost no capacity beyond the array that already holds them (empyrean §5.1, which corrects an earlier `tiles + animated slots <= 448` rule that would have told Aurora the flagship act cannot carry any band at all).
invariants.layoutTileIndex: layout[row*64 + col] is a nametable word whose low LAYOUT_TILE_INDEX_MASK bits are a blob-local index into `tiles` and whose remaining bits are attributes the consumer preserves — EXCEPT that a word of exactly 0 is passed through unrebased and renders VRAM tile 0 (blank) rather than tiles[0]. Adding or removing a band renumbers `tiles`, so every nonzero word must be rewritten INDEX-ONLY, and a rewrite that would produce the value 0 is unrepresentable rather than merely different.
invariants.slotOrder: WRITER OBLIGATION 1, and the consumer CANNOT CHECK IT. Band cell (c, r) is slot `slot_base + c*rows + r` on a HORIZONTAL band (column-major) and `slot_base + r*cols + c` on a VERTICAL one (ROW-major). It lives in `layout` — which cell references which slot — and the same set of slots reads as a scroll under one order and as a shimmer under the other. aeon: 'a band's slots are deduped against the static blob and appear at many cells — so nothing checks this'. Any Aurora assertion over the SET, the COUNT or a CHECKSUM of a band's slots is vacuous here by construction; only the ORDER discriminates.
invariants.phaseAxis: WRITER OBLIGATION 2. The eight phase banks must be translations ALONG THE DECLARED AXIS. aeon refuses exactly one case and admits everything else: a vertical band whose phases are exact HORIZONTAL translations of phase 0 and are not also vertical ones (`validate_band_phase_axis`) — the reachable accident of a horizontal-only shift-fill run over a band declared vertical. Composites are deliberately admitted on both axes, because the shipped horizontal bands are composites rather than pure rolls.
invariants.axisRoundTrip: WRITER OBLIGATION 3. `axis` must survive a load / edit-something-else / save. Dropping it silently reverts the band to horizontal, and obligation 2's guard cannot see a band that no longer claims to be vertical. Absent means "horizontal", and Aurora never writes the default in — a save of an untouched document is not a diff.

amendments.what: THE MOTION AXIS (aeon EFFECTS-W1 DoD item 8, merged as chain 210). Adds `bandKeys.axis`; RENAMES invariant `columnBytesPowerOfTwo` -> `rotationUnitPowerOfTwo` and `patternWidth` -> `patternPeriod`, because both rules now read off a DIFFERENT band key per axis; and adds the three writer obligations the consumer explicitly cannot check (`slotOrder`, `phaseAxis`, `axisRoundTrip`). No engine byte moved: the vertical arm reuses the same whole-unit DMA rotate, so the power-of-two rule keeps its SHAPE and changes only which key it is spelled on.
